title: Ameimar bar Mar Yenuka
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned by this name in [Chullin 18b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.18b.12), where he said, “I was standing before Rabbi Chiyya son of Rav Avya.” But he is also mentioned as Ameimar without further designation, and he is bar Mar Yenuka, as in [Gittin 19b](https://www.sefaria.org/Gittin.19b.17): Ravina reports that Ameimar told him what Mareimar had said in Rav Dimi’s name. Hyman considers this Ameimar undoubtedly bar Mar Yenuka, for the first Ameimar would not say to Ravina, “Thus said Mareimar,” since Mareimar was much later than Ameimar and headed the academy in Sura after Rav Ashi. This Ravina is the later Ravina bar Rav Huna, and this Ameimar is bar Mar Yenuka, who said to the later Ravina, “Thus said Mareimar.” Hyman regards this as clear.

Likewise we find in [Ketubot 21b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.21b.1): “Rav Yehudah said that Shmuel said: A witness and a judge combine. Rami bar Chama said: How excellent is this teaching! Ravnai came … he said: Thus said Shmuel: A witness and a judge combine. Ameimar said: How excellent is this teaching! Rav Ashi said to Ameimar: Because your mother’s father praised it, you too praise it?” Hyman considers it impossible that this Ameimar is Ameimar without further designation, since Rav Ashi was Rami bar Chama’s son-in-law, as in Beitzah 29a (compare [Beitzah 29b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.29b.5)); how then could Ameimar, Rav Ashi’s teacher, who died long before Rav Ashi, be Rami bar Chama’s grandson?

Hyman therefore considers him undoubtedly Ameimar bar Mar Yenuka, and from this he infers his lineage: his father Mar Yenuka married Rami bar Chama’s daughter and was Rav Ashi’s brother-in-law, and Ameimar his son had Rav Ashi as an uncle by marriage, and he was indeed much younger than Rav Ashi.

Hyman states that this is not Mar Yenuka son of Rav Chisda but the son of Mar Zutra, as cited in the Ra’avad’s Kabbalah. He is likewise mentioned in [Menachot 66a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.66a.16): “The Rabbis of Rav Ashi’s school counted,” etc.; “Ameimar counted days.” Hyman infers from the arrangement of the Talmud that he is the later Ameimar.

His death is mentioned in the [Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon 1:110](https://www.sefaria.org/Epistle_of_Rav_Sherira_Gaon.1.110), part 3, chapter 3 in Hyman’s numbering:[^4] in year 781 (תשפ״א; era unspecified here) Ameimar bar Mar Yenuka, Huna Mar son of the Exilarch, and Mesharshiya bar Pekod were imprisoned, and in Adar of that year he was killed; and this was 33 years after Rav Ashi’s death.[^3]

notes.text: All undoubtedly/clear force stays within Hyman’s argument for late Ameimar and Ravina; Mareimar’s academy headship is not kingship. The father-in-law/uncle-by-marriage inference and alternative MarYenuka filiation remain explicitly his, not a new genealogy merge. תשפ״א is781 with no era supplied here;33years is the stated interval, not converted.

The consulted Ketubot 21b has Ameimar praise the teaching, Ashi refer to his mother’s father and then say Rava had already refuted it. Hyman’s quotation is abridged and is not expanded from this continuation. The passage does not independently settle his late-Ameimar/Ravina equation, uncle-by-marriage inference or Mar Yenuka filiation. His undoubtedly/clear force, Talmud-arrangement argument, reported 781 and 33-year interval remain as stated, without an added era conversion.

In Gittin, Ravina reports what Ameimar told him from Mareimar in Rav Dimi’s name. Ketubot refers to Ameimar’s maternal grandfather without naming him in Rav Ashi’s reply. The statement that Rav Ashi’s wife was Rami bar Chama’s daughter is found at Beitzah 29b. Hyman’s reconstruction of Ameimar’s lineage and chronology remains his argument.

The consulted Oxford 1888 text places Ameimar’s imprisonment in Tevet of 781 and his execution in Adar of that year. It names the exilarch as Huna son of Mar Zutra. The thirty-three-year interval is Hyman’s calculation.
